answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through completed escrowed trades with distinct counterparties, while weighting each counterparty by time-tested stake and limiting how much one identity can contribute to another’s score. Spinning up a hundred aliases then adds little: the attacker must fund each escrow and recruit or simulate genuinely independent trading partners, who can refuse to release payment. The harbor ledger may look like a grove threaded through karst, but its costly, reciprocal history is what makes fake identities hard to manufacture.
